text: Now I have the geometry. Let me plan and start building the outbound section (station, lift, big drop, airtime hills).
Outbound built. Now the far turn and return leg with a vertical-loop field.
Circuit closed. Let me test it and bank a score.
Banked 7.01 (ride time was short — only 64s). Let me rebuild with a long slow top section and more content to raise excitement.
Height misalignment — I'll rebuild with an exactly-counted lift.
Off by 8 x due to a loop miscount. Undo the final turn and insert two loops.
Closed. Testing v2.
v2 intensity hit 10.5 — that tanks the score. Reverting to the 240-height profile with more length.
v3 scored 7.21 — intensity at the 10 cap. Let me try a taller drop with a softened (25°) runout to keep g-forces down.
Lift count slipped again. Rebuilding with an exact 18-piece lift and verifying.
Tall drops push intensity over the cliff. Let me test whether a long slow top-flat run (as in the 7.38 design) raises ride time and excitement.
v5 = 7.21 at safer intensity 9.56. The 7.38 design had a ~33-unit drop. Let me try a 272-height drop (16 lift pieces) plus long top flats.
Lift landed at 15 pieces (H=256) — still a bigger drop. Adapting the descent to the actual height.
Same 7.2. The 7.38 design used boosters — let me test whether boosters add excitement.
Boosters added a little (7.24). Let me try a tall drop with a mid-course brake to keep intensity under 10.
The brake caused a valley/runaway — no score. Let me carefully build an H=272 version, verifying the lift count in two steps.
H=272 confirmed. Now the top flats, drop, and outbound hills.
New best: 7.26. Let me push further — more top flats and 10 inversions.
7.32 now. Let me push the slow top run further with 24 flats.
Best so far: 7.33. Let me confirm the banked result.

Banked: **steel twister, excitement 7.33** (intensity 9.74, 10 inversions, 1042 length, similarity 0.36) — a 272-high chain lift drops into a 33-unit plunge, sweeping hills, a far U-turn, and a 10-loop inversion field with boosters.
